entries.title: Argentina's bid to stop Falkland Islands oil drilling rejected
entries.snippet: A joint venture between UK-Israeli companies is set to start exploring for oil and gas, but Argentina sought to block it as part of its claim to sovereignty.

entries.title: Two staff killed in Israeli strike on Gaza medical clinic, MSF says
entries.snippet: The Israeli military says it targeted "Hamas terrorists" in the strike which has been condemned by the World Health Organization.

entries.title: Afghanistan explosion kills 10 students and injures more than 100, official says
entries.snippet: A spokesman for Afghanistan's interior ministry says the blast was caused by carelessness at an explosives depot nearby.

entries.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wants to defy the polls, and his main rivals accuse him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal".

entries.title: OpenAI counter-sues Apple over alleged theft of trade secrets
entries.snippet: The ChatGPT-maker alleges that tech giant Apple stole trade secrets through a former employee.

entries.title: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
entries.snippet: The pilot was the sole survivor of the crash during a rescue mission in a remote area known for drug trafficking.

entries.title: Australian wrestler Bronson Reed dies aged 38, WWE says
entries.snippet: Tributes have flooded in for the 38-year-old Australian who is survived by his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter.

entries.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
entries.snippet: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.

entries.title: Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
entries.snippet: The headquarters of Halk TV were raided last month, the latest in a series of crackdowns on news sources deemed critical of the government.

entries.title: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.

entries.title: 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
entries.snippet: Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.

entries.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
entries.snippet: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

entries.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
entries.snippet: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing his followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

entries.title: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
entries.snippet: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia has not.

entries.snippet: The Ukrainian president tells the BBC that Russia's Vladimir Putin should not be treated as a friend.

entries.snippet: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

entries.title: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
entries.snippet: Ukraine settles in for another devastating winter as the questions persists: how will it all end?

entries.title: Explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan kills 7, wounds more than 90
entries.snippet: Local officials said the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for mining explosives.

entries.title: New wave of Democratic attorneys general may reshape the justice system
entries.snippet: The Democratic victories could have major effects for what alleged crimes are investigated, lawsuits filed and court cases heard across the U.S.

entries.title: Sudan's lost generation: War is stealing the childhood of millions
entries.snippet: Three years of war have stolen childhood from millions of children in Sudan, leaving them displaced, hungry and fighting for survival instead of learning in a classroom.

entries.snippet: A powerful storm knocked out power for nearly 1 million customers and flooded streets. And, experts predict inflation will not dampen American spending for the holidays

entries.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
entries.snippet: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

entries.title: From Thanksgiving blackouts to Black Friday, a holiday hit by wild weather and economic woes
entries.snippet: A storm battered much of the country on Thursday, knocking out power to thousands of homes and disrupting travel. Today, Black Friday shopping deals kick off, and on Saturday New York City will hold the postponed Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

entries.title: Can luxury save Macy's?
entries.snippet: This week's celebration of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving parade finds the department store at a turning point. After years of losing sales, the retailer is reimagining itself — as a higher-end destination.

entries.title: Screen-free tweens try their hand at Dungeons & Dragons
entries.snippet: Some parents, fed up with screens, have found an analog oasis in the role-playing game invented in the 1970s.

entries.title: 12 strategies to cut your risk of dementia. Take this quiz to start
entries.snippet: Here's something you can do as you gather with family and friends this holiday season: Take a free, five-minute quiz to assess your brain health. You'll learn simple changes to keep your mind sharp.

entries.title: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it
entries.snippet: Trump's sweeping immigration changes — an asylum ban, mass firings and new legal maneuvers — have all but ended asylum. The high court will soon consider whether some shifts deny people due process.

entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Nick Schifrin to discuss the week in politics, including President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin, Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia and sweeping new tariffs on China, Europe and others.

entries.title: A veteran's Brief But Spectacular take on finding new ways to serve after the military
entries.snippet: Nancy Preston, a veteran, helped aspiring food entrepreneurs start their own businesses after her time in the U.S. military. She shares her Brief But Spectacular take on finding new ways to serve.

entries.title: Protesters take to the streets in Puerto Rico's capital as standard of living deteriorates

entries.title: Mexico's government is slamming a DEA crime tip line as foreign interference. Others are thrilled.
entries.snippet: The announcement opened the latest chapter in an ongoing struggle between the U.S. and Mexican governments over who has the right to take action against cartels in Mexico.

entries.title: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds a Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
entries.snippet: The 2019 law, known as Bill 21, bans religious symbols — including Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses — for workers covered by it.

entries.title: Army deems lead azide detonation a success but criticism lingers over notification

entries.title: U.S. military says it disabled another ship that tried to breach naval blockade on Iranian ports
entries.snippet: A military aircraft fired "precision munitions" at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, and the "ship's propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed," U.S. Central Command said in a statement.

entries.title: Using a drone and a poop-sniffing dog, scientists perform health checks on endangered orcas
entries.snippet: In their search for their dwindling food source, the whales are spending less time in the Salish Sea, the maze of inland waters between Washington State and British Columbia.

entries.title: A Ukraine loan is in limbo after EU budget talks stall. Leaders will try again
entries.snippet: The spending package is small compared to national budgets — around 1% to 1.2% of gross national income — but it encapsulates the ambitions of the world's biggest trading bloc and how it sees itself on the international stage.

entries.title: NFL's Thanksgiving tripleheader has impressive comebacks and fantastic finishes
entries.snippet: Caleb Williams put the Chicago Bears in first place. Joe Milton III put a dagger in his former team's season. Tyler Bass put the Buffalo Bills in position for a No. 1 seed.

entries.title: Republicans rethink tariffs, giving Democrats an opening to challenge Trump
entries.snippet: After devastating election losses that centered on rising costs, many Republicans said they're open to reconsidering some of the levies that have become a central plank of Trump's global trade agenda.

entries.title: Los Angeles schools block Google's AI features, consider dropping tech giant's products
entries.snippet: The LA district, which enrolls half a million students, has made no formal announcement, and the move caught parents and students by surprise, said Bridie Lee, a leader of Schools Beyond Screens LA.

entries.title: Serbia's student movement proposes a chemistry professor for presidency ahead of Dec. 27 ballot
entries.snippet: The presidential vote comes after the student movement defeated former President Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early parliamentary ballot on Oct. 25.

entries.title: Zelenskyy urges the U.S. to pressure Putin, calling Trump's 'my friend' remark strange
entries.snippet: "He can't be a friend," Zelenskyy told the BBC in Kyiv, likening it to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II.

entries.title: Parts of the U.S. clean up, power outages being restored after Thanksgiving storm soaks East Coast
entries.snippet: The storms snarled travel and downed trees and power lines. The heavy weather led to water rescues from New York to Virginia.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: As Spain votes, what could change for Europe?
entries.snippet: Spain votes on Sunday. A loss for Pedro Sanchez and a shift to the right in Madrid could affect how one of the EU's largest countries approaches migration, defense and the war in Gaza.

entries.title: Germany news: Job market unlikely to recover before summer
entries.snippet: The head of Germany's employment agency said employment would remain at its current level for a while. Meanwhile, electric vehicle sales are expected to pass 1 million next year. DW has more.

entries.title: Afghanistan: Several killed in blast near middle school
entries.snippet: Officials have said improperly stored explosives at a mining site ignited, damaging nearby buildings including a school. An investigation is ongoing.

entries.title: India: Hindu lamp lighting at disputed Thiruparankundram pillar today
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court has directed that the Tamil Hindu ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit today at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
entries.snippet: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.

entries.title: Polls close in Taiwan's closely watched local elections
entries.snippet: Campaigners have stayed away from the topic of China and focused on issues like transport and childcare. Still, Beijing had put pressure on the progressive candidate for Taipei mayor, who ended up losing the race.

entries.title: Spain's Sanchez makes final appeal to voters before election
entries.snippet: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told people to turn out in large numbers so the country does not go "backwards." Polls suggest an end to his eight-year leftist leadership of Spain.

entries.title: US disables ship in Gulf of Oman under Iran blockade
entries.snippet: The United States said it was continuing "to strictly enforce the blockade" of Iran's ports. Meanwhile, Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over a strike that killed two Italian technicians.

entries.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
entries.snippet: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.

entries.title: Germany news: Lawmakers approve debt-laden 2027 budget
entries.snippet: German lawmakers voted on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spending. Elsewhere, the Left Party is hosting a summit on femicide and the BSW party conference starts in Dresden. DW has more.

entries.title: Spanish rider Marc Marquez announces MotoGP retirement, days after clinching record 8th world title
entries.snippet: Marc Marquez took fans and his team by surprise when announcing this weekend's race in Valencia will be his last. The 33-year-old won a record eight MotoGP titles, including his rookie and retirement seasons.

entries.title: France seeks German man in Channel migrant boat probe
entries.snippet: A German businessman is accused of supplying equipment to smugglers organizing migrant crossings from France to the United Kingdom. However, he can't face formal charges until he is extradited to France.

entries.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
entries.snippet: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.

entries.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, Brussels' most anticipated new art museum, opens its doors
entries.snippet: A major addition to Europe's cultural scene: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, the new contemporary art museum in a former Citroen factory complex, is celebrating its opening with a free, nonstop weekend program.

entries.title: Serbia's Student List runs chemistry professor Radomir Saicic for president
entries.snippet: After ousting strongman Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's student movement has now nominated academic Radomir Saicic for the upcoming presidential vote. Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of trying to collapse the state.

entries.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
entries.snippet: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.

entries.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
entries.snippet: Thailand is seeking to tackle river pollution stemming from rare earth mines in neighboring Myanmar. The two countries held joint talks this week as a "first step towards agreeing on the evidence."

entries.title: Georgia: Police clash with Besiktas fans at Israel club game
entries.snippet: Turkey's Besiktas accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate" force during the game with Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva, which saw Besiktas fans unfurl a banner supporting Palestine.

entries.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
entries.snippet: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.
